What I think is that most people don't realize (and I'm not assuming my opinion is better here) is that downvoating is not only a way to repress bad content but it's also very important to bring the best content to the top. Take this post here: 20 comments in an hour, could become 40 in 2. Most people won't read all 40 comments but almost all of them are "fine". If everyone upvotes the "fine" then they will all have similar scores and the best comments could be buried under there. If just one or two people though downvote mediocre posts it makes sure that the best will be on top - where they should be.

Another point is that if everyone upvotes the "fine" then the top posts will usually be the earlier ones (which gathered more "fine votes") and not the best ones. And that is what we usually see in posts with lots of comments.

Not sure I explained this very well but anyway - downvotes have a "positive" effect too, they don't need to be used only on extreme cases. Overall I'd like to see more people using their downvotes responsibly - this becomes so much more important if Voat grows and starts having hundreds of comments per post...
